HP:0000478.label: Abnormality of the eye
HP:0000478.text: very early onset severe eye disease

records.label: Two sibs with Knobloch syndrome

phenotypes.text: very early onset severe eye disease

quotes: We report on two sibs with high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration (VRD), and occipital encephalocoele or scalp lesion.
One case presents with very early onset of severe eye disease, whereas the other is notable for the very mild scalp defect. In addition, both appear to have an unusual pulmonary lymphatic condition.

records.label: New Zealand family
records.segregation: Linkage to the COL18A1 locus was excluded
quotes: Linkage to the COL18A1 locus was excluded in the New Zealand family, providing evidence for the existence of a second KNO locus.

Analysis of two unrelated KNO families from Hungary and New Zealand allowed us to confirm the involvement of COL18A1 in the pathogenesis of KNO and to demonstrate the existence of genetic heterogeneity.

records.label: KNO2 family (historical pedigree, two affected sibs)
records.segregation: Monoallelic and apparently de novo in both affected sibs; absent from normal parents' blood DNA, suggesting parental germline mosaicism
quotes: We studied an historical pedigree (published in 1998) designated as KNO2 (Knobloch type 2 syndrome with intellectual disability, autistic behavior, retinal degeneration, encephalocele).
Whole exome sequencing of the two affected siblings and the normal parents resulted in the identification of a PAK2 non-synonymous substitution p.(Glu435Lys) as a causative variant.

The variant was monoallelic and apparently de novo in both siblings indicating a likely germ-line mosaicism in one of the parents; the mosaicism, however, could not be observed after deep sequencing of blood parental DNA.

notes.statement: Antonarakis et al. (2021) found that the PAK2 Glu435Lys variant, located in the kinase domain, was predicted by structural analysis to possibly compromise kinase activity, and in transfected HEK293T cells it caused a partial loss of kinase activity.
quotes: Structural analysis of the PAK2 p.(Glu435Lys) variant that is located in the kinase domain of the protein predicts a possible compromise in the kinase activity.
Functional analysis of the p.(Glu435Lys) PAK2 variant in transfected HEK293T cells results in a partial loss of the kinase activity.

notes.statement: Antonarakis et al. (2021) concluded that KNO2 in the studied family was dominant, with the apparently de novo variant in both sibs indicating likely germline mosaicism in a parent.
quotes: We conclude that the KNO2 syndrome in the studied family is dominant and caused by a deleterious variant in the PAK2 gene.

notes.statement: Menzel et al. (2004) excluded linkage to the COL18A1 locus in a Knobloch syndrome family from New Zealand. This was evidence for a second Knobloch syndrome locus, which they named KNO2.
quotes: Linkage to the COL18A1 locus was excluded in the New Zealand family, providing evidence for the existence of a second KNO locus.
We named the second unmapped locus for Knobloch syndrome KNO2.

notes.statement: Menzel et al. (2004) used mutation analysis to exclude COL15A1, a multiplexin collagen similar to COL18A1, as the gene responsible for KNO2.
quotes: Mutation analysis excluded COL15A1, a member of the multiplexin collagen subfamily similar to COL18A1, as being responsible for KNO2.

notes.statement: Menzel et al. (2004) described Knobloch syndrome as an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.
quotes: Knobloch syndrome (KNO) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, and congenital encephalocele.

notes.statement: Wilson et al. (1998) reviewed the literature on Knobloch syndrome and suggested that mesoderm might be involved in the morphogenesis of the disorder.
quotes: We review the literature on Knobloch syndrome, discuss possible causes, and suggest a possible involvement of mesoderm in the morphogenesis.
